data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The reliability gain is genuine if and only if perturbing the checklist's decision-relevant features while preserving its formal structure degrades panel accuracy less than it degrades a hypothetical single expert forced to use the same perturbed rule; mere compliance is distinguished by showing panel accuracy collapses synchronously with checklist-feature alignment, proving the panel adds no independent signal beyond checklist execution.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The evaluation does not include a perturbation or degradation component, making it impossible to distinguish orthogonal signal from compliance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel relies on un-encodable tacit knowledge that the checklist does not capture but that nonetheless tracks the right answer, meaning the checklist is epiphenomenal rather than the panel.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is perfectly complete and lossless relative to the domain, in which case there is no 'mere compliance' to distinguish from genuine understanding.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist is a lossy linear projection of the full feature space: it cannot distinguish genuine understanding from correlated compliance. Genuine reliability gain requires the panel to contribute a residual signal orthogonal to the checklist itself. The within-evaluation test forces this separation by perturbing checklist features: if the panel's accuracy degrades identically to a rule-bound automaton, the panel is epiphenomenal to the checklist (mere compliance). If the panel maintains accuracy via un-encoded features, the gain is genuine. This follows the covering principle that reliability is a property of the combined system, not the checklist artifact alone, and any valid test must isolate the system's generative contribution from its procedural mimicry.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
